item.title: Taj Aims for 20 Hotels in Middle East Over 5 Years
item.description: The Indian hotel group is focusing on steady expansion in UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, and select GCC markets.

item.title: What a Siberian Startup and a Saudi Ticketing App Reveal About Travel’s Future
item.description: Two startups from two different worlds are quietly rewriting the rules of who controls the travel transaction, with fascinating implications.

item.title: TBO’s North America Deal Begins to Show Up in the Numbers
item.description: The Classic Vacations acquisition hands TBO a new distribution footprint. It brings higher-value bookings and deep industry relationships. But that also means that TBO’s numbers will look messy until the integration is done.

item.title: Hilton CEO: 2026 ‘Will Be a Lot Better Than 25’ After Results Show Sluggish Growth
item.description: Hilton’s muted growth in revenue per available room last year primarily reflected an economic strain on mid-market travelers. Yet CEO Chris Nassetta is optimistic about what he's seeing in the overall bookings data for 2026.

item.title: New Frontier Airlines CEO Outlines Path to Shore Up Profits, Eyes In-Flight Wi-Fi Launch
item.description: New Frontier CEO James Dempsey wants to take the carrier back to its low-cost roots, saying that saving on costs will lead Frontier to a more sustainable path.

item.title: U.S. Travel From Canada Falls Again to Start 2026
item.description: The decline in visitors from Canada that hit the U.S. travel industry hard in 2025 shows no signs of slowing down.

item.title: Marriott Says Google AI Mode Will Process Hotel Bookings, Not Just Send Links
item.description: Marriott is the first major hotel to publicly discuss its work with Google on its upcoming agentic AI travel booking tool. But it raises more questions than answers — especially whether AI Mode offers in-chat checkout for partners and link-outs for everyone else.

item.title: New Marriott and Hilton Filings Reveal Risks From AI Platforms to Direct Bookings
item.description: Artificial intelligence isn’t charging hotels commissions yet. But lawyers at Marriott and Hilton are already preparing for a world where AI platforms could become the next powerful gatekeepers in travel distribution.

item.title: India’s Digital Payments Boom Reaches Foreign Shores
item.description: The world is no longer expecting Indian travelers to adapt during their travels, and is ready to cater to them instead.

item.title: Comcast Partners With Adara to Measure How TV Ads Drive Travel Bookings — Exclusive
item.description: Comcast and Adara have a new bid to give travel marketers what TV has rarely offered: a credible line from ad exposure to bookings and revenue. Now it’s time to see if it can scale.
